# How Do I Manage Maintenance Contracts With Third Parties?


You manage third-party maintenance contracts by keeping each agreement versioned and connected to the vendor and properties it covers, with automated renewal alerts. On **Jestor** , this combines versioned contract records with the vendor registry.


Short stay operators accumulate multiple maintenance contracts, pool, landscaping, air conditioning, quickly, and without structure these agreements end up scattered with no clear link back to the relevant properties or dates.


## What complicates third-party maintenance contract management


- Contracts stored separately from the specific properties they cover
- No automatic alert when a contract is approaching renewal
- Scope and value terms retyped manually into a separate tracker
- No connection between the contract and the actual maintenance history performed


## How structured contract management works


- Maintenance contracts stay versioned, connected to the vendor and covered properties
- **OCR** can read the contract and pre-fill key terms, scope, value, dates
- Automations can flag contracts approaching renewal or expiration
- Maintenance history performed connects to the same vendor and contract


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Version history removes ambiguity about which contract copy is current
- OCR removes manual retyping of key terms
- The connection between contract, vendor, and property gives full visibility
- Automated alerts replace the dependency on manually checking dates

## Frequently Asked Questions


**Does this replace legal review of the contract?** No, it structures the process, legal review still applies where needed. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can one contract cover multiple properties?** Yes, records can be connected relationally to more than one property.


**Does maintenance history connect to the correct contract?** Yes, if structured as related records.
